title: Improving Multi-modal Recommender Systems by Denoising and Aligning Multi-modal Content and User Feedback

problem.claim: Multi-modal recommender systems must address noisy multi-modal content, noisy user feedback, and alignment between multi-modal content and user feedback.

gap.claim: Previous studies overlook noisy multi-modal content, noisy user feedback, and alignment between multi-modal content and user feedback.

contributions.claim: DA-MRS constructs item-item graphs using consistent content similarity across modalities to mitigate noise in multi-modal content.
DA-MRS associates observed-feedback probability with multi-modal content and uses a denoised BPR loss to denoise user feedback.
DA-MRS uses user-preference-guided alignment and graded-item-relation-guided alignment to improve task-specific item representation and provide finer-grained alignment.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments showing that DA-MRS is a plug-and-play framework.
The authors report significant and consistent improvements across various datasets, backbone models, and noisy scenarios.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multi-modal recommender systems are important across diverse online web platforms.
Prior studies overlook noise in multi-modal content, noise in user feedback, and alignment between content and feedback.
The paper proposes DA-MRS to address these challenges.
DA-MRS denoises content and feedback and applies two forms of alignment.
The authors report improvements across datasets, backbone models, and noisy scenarios.

source_observation.claim: The framework combines content denoising, feedback denoising, and task-specific alignment.

interpretation.claim: Robust recommendation may benefit from addressing noise and cross-modal or cross-signal alignment jointly.

application.claim: When recommendation inputs contain noisy modalities and feedback, consider separating denoising mechanisms from alignment mechanisms within a unified framework.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these mechanisms are beneficial for settings outside the reported datasets, backbone models, and noisy scenarios.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, backbone models, noise-generation procedures, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not provide implementation details, computational costs, ablation results, or reproducibility information.
